attributes.nuance_translation: A polite expression used for suggesting mutual activities, that has an indirect nuance of an invitation.

attributes.body:
As covered in our ましょう lesson, ましょう is one of the conjugations of the auxiliary verb ます, and is a common (polite) way to suggest that something be done 'together'.

Adding the particle か to this expression simply changes the nuance from 'let's', to 'shall we?', and is more of a direct question than ましょう by itself.

Like ましょう, this expression can be added to the ます stem form of any verb.

One thing to note with these examples is that they are 'suggestions', not 'invitations'. In Japanese there is a slight difference between the two, in the same way that there is in English. If you want to invite someone to do something, the most natural way would be to use ませんか, a phrase that is similar to ましょうか.

The difference here is that 'won't you do (A)?' has a stronger nuance of being a direct invitation, while ましょうか is closer to just 'let's do (A)!'

attributes.description: ましょう and ましょうか
Making a motion to do something using the volitional form (polite)

attributes.body: Both ～ましょうか and ましょう are polite expressions used to suggest or propose an action. ましょう is more assertive, similar to 'Let's (do this)' in English. In contrast, ～ましょうか is softer and seeks the listener's approval or agreement, like 'Shall I...?' or 'Shall we...?' ましょう can also function as a gentle command, such as when a teacher says 'Let's be quiet' to mean 'Be quiet.'

ましょうか and Verb [よう] are both volitional forms, with ましょうか being polite and Verb [よう] (sometimes with か) casual. ～ましょうか is used to make polite suggestions like 'Shall we...?' (e.g. 行きましょうか = 'Shall we go?') 行こうか is more casual and introspective, often expressing the speaker's internal thoughts (e.g. 'Should I go?')

ましょう and ませんか are both polite forms based on the ます form and used to make suggestions or invitations. ましょう typically suggests doing something together (e.g. 食べましょう = 'Let's eat'), while ませんか invites the listener to join (e.g. 食べませんか = 'Won't you eat [some]?') ましょう is more assertive, while ませんか is softer and more inviting.
